feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, the experience progression is logical, and the scope feels substantial. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior narrative: strong headline, relevant summary, and excellent career progression within NACo culminating in leadership and consulting roles.  
- Good evidence of scale and impact: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add credibility.  
- Broad but coherent skill set across strategy, governance, web platforms, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; consolidate overlapping sections to improve scannability and structure.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scope metrics: e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption improvements, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; maintain consistent punctuation in bullets; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; consider standardizing date format (“Sept.” vs “Mar.”/“Oct.”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and sharpen the opening: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years’ experience modernizing public-sector web ecosystems, governance, and content operations.”
- Add specific scale/impact from recent roles, e.g., “Led modernization of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Replace broad phrasing like “building the platforms” with more direct verbs: “modernizing,” “scaling,” “leading,” “designing.”
- Consider a cleaner rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector websites, governance models, and editorial operations. Leads enterprise web transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, multimedia systems, and AI-enabled content discovery for mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled content discovery.”
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely repeats the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinct and executive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and trim wording: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership”
- Replace broader or repetitive items with sharper, outcome-oriented terms: “AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration”
- Consider elevating “Advocacy and public-sector communications” to “Public-sector advocacy communications” for cleaner phrasing.
- Refine the final item to “Multimedia production and livestream operations” or “Studio, video, and livestream operations” if you want stronger differentiation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” analytics, and multimedia are already prominent in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; consider swapping in a less repeated strength such as “Cross-functional digital leadership.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats several themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp line with parallel structure.
- Replace generic verbs (“Built,” “Developed”) with more specific ones where possible: “Launched,” “Architected,” “Produced,” “Delivered.”
- Clarify unique value in each project: e.g., “AI chat at bill level,” “Drupal 10 microsite,” “10×20-foot conference installation,” “recurring cross-channel advocacy series.”
- If available, add 1 measurable result across the block (usage, engagement, campaign reach, or adoption).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with NACo experience bullets; keep this block focused on named examples, not responsibilities.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “distribution across website, email and social,” and Drupal platform work are already echoed elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten around highest-value outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-led bullets, e.g.:
- “Built and optimized cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Provided hands-on CMS/front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, time saved, or engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “Drupal/web improvement” repeat heavily from the 2022–2024 NACo role; frame this entry as post-staff consulting leadership and new initiatives.
- The microsite and AI search bullets overlap with Recent Projects; keep the CV item higher-level if those projects stay detailed elsewhere.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in the adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope-and-impact line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and organization-wide communications operations.”
- Combine the website bullets and foreground outcome: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more results-based: add email/social performance if available (growth, engagement, CTR, list size, campaign output) instead of “reaching tens of thousands.”
- Tighten remaining bullets with action + result phrasing: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal capacity for advocacy programming, events and recurring video content”; “Expanded analytics stack… to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video-program growth also appears in earlier roles; focus here on building the studio and scaling organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Tighten it around what was uniquely expanded here: recurring newsletter operations, advocacy video, and cross-team editorial coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + distinct contribution: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and publishing consistency.
- If possible, add outcomes: email open/click rates, video views, production volume, turnaround time, or stakeholder adoption.
- Replace weak phrasing like “helped improve” and “helping scale” with direct ownership verbs: “improved,” “standardized,” “expanded,” “established.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” duplicates the Director role; keep this version more execution- and systems-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the prior role; frame this entry as formalizing/scaling the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Make it sharper, more senior, and less generic by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than broad communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic labels with tighter, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better reflect your recent leadership scope.
- Add one stronger differentiator if space allows, e.g. “Stakeholder-aligned digital governance” or “Mission-driven platform strategy.”
- Keep terminology consistent with recent roles: “governance,” “cross-channel,” and “enterprise” align well with 2022–present experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicates “Multi-channel communication” in Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already echoed in the header and multiple NACo entries.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent execution strengths tied to your NACo work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal platform delivery • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths first: put Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and workflow automation ahead of older/general platforms.
- Drop weaker or dated phrasing like “jQuery” unless required by target roles; it lowers the strategic tone.
- If space allows, add light impact context: “Drupal platform delivery for large public-facing sites” or “AI-enabled search and discovery design.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” is already repeated in “Technical + IT”; avoid mirroring the same list here.
- “CMS modernization” and “workflow automation” also echo Core Competencies, so keep this version more execution-focused.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic application and business value over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization.”
- Tighten to 5–7 items and group tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace weaker phrases with outcome-oriented ones: “KPI framework development,” “executive/leadership dashboards,” “performance and search optimization”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity - KPI framework development - Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting - SEO, user behavior and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly; keep detailed tool inventory there and make this section more strategic.
- “Leadership reporting” also overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo multimedia bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and tied to the in-house studio/event capability highlighted in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace bullets with tighter, higher-level phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- PTZ camera and studio system operations  
- Virtual event delivery and technical coordination
- If space allows, sharpen one bullet to reflect leadership scope: **In-house studio buildout and broadcast workflow management**
- Keep wording outcome-oriented and operational rather than tool-list-like.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps with **Core Competencies: “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”** Consider keeping the broader phrase there and using this item for more specific studio/event capabilities.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close; combine to avoid repetition.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same message.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize depth and recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, order by strongest/recentest platform first and consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project.
- Add light qualifiers only where credible and relevant, e.g., “Drupal 10” or “enterprise publishing environments,” rather than listing tools flatly.
- If you want this section purely technical, rename to “CMS & Web Publishing Platforms” for clearer alignment.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2], which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent experience; avoid repeating it in multiple sections without adding context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modernize/clarify the tooling.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & Technical Implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent work; if kept, place last or label as legacy support.
- Consider grouping by function for readability: **Front-end:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript | **Integrations & tagging:** APIs, Google Tag Manager | **Edge/DevOps:** Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If space allows elsewhere, tie tools to outcomes in recent roles (e.g., “used for CMS enhancements, tagging deployment, workflow automation, and edge-based web improvements”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Technical Implementation” may also overlap with automation/workflow items if GitHub Actions is described elsewhere.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and grouped to signal actual operating strength.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and trim lower-value collaboration tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Put the strongest, most relevant systems first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If accurate, add a light proficiency cue in the heading or formatting, e.g. “Automation & Workflow Systems: Airtable (system design), Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana…”
- Consider dropping Slack/Teams entirely if space is tight; they are expected and don’t add much differentiation for a senior digital leader.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar signals—listing all four may feel padded unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a generic tool list. Strengthen it by signaling enterprise-scale email/engagement capability and aligning the wording with the CV’s public-sector communications focus.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/context rather than more tools: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation and member communications**
- Keep platform names only if these were used meaningfully in recent roles; otherwise prioritize the systems most tied to NACo email/newsletter leadership

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies and repeated email references across multiple NACo roles; avoid adding generic phrases like “email strategy” here unless tied to platform capability
- If Dynamics 365 or Mailchimp were not central in recent work, listing all three may dilute the stronger Higher Logic/email-operations story

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the Director role. Make it sharper by emphasizing methods/capabilities, not just repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation & dashboarding**
- Replace “A/B testing” with **Experimentation** if formal testing was limited; it reads broader and more credible.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with **Executive/leadership reporting** or **KPI design** to signal business impact, not just tool use.
- Order by strongest/recent tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Clarity, then analytical capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section; consider trimming one or making this version more tool-focused while the other stays outcome/capability-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating the exact same phrasing.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer outcomes: mention size/scope of the website refresh, frequency of livestreams/video updates, or growth in content capacity/engagement if available.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables such as “produced livestreams, weekly video updates and multimedia content for advocacy and member communications.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped onboard and guide…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as launching or piloting the format.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version lighter and more execution-oriented.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a stronger action/result version: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, creating a new multimedia channel for member and policy communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats themes covered more strongly in later digital roles.
- Avoid overemphasizing general communications support; later entries already establish that progression.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and keep workflow/production capabilities in experience or topline skills.
